title: Competitor
description: A person's master record for one competitor or one alternative, at <venture>/competitors/<id>.json. A competitor is a company serving the same customers with an offering that can replace the venture's (Porter 1980). An alternative is what the customer does in its place, doing nothing included (kind alternative). A person owns it. Besides the name it may hold what the offering is, whom it is for, its published price, what it does and does not do next to the venture's product, the sources read with their dates, the basis of the claim, the stance and a prediction of its next move; all of these are optional. The signal projector may create it once when it is missing, from a signal's organization part, and never writes it again (everything-ecosystem docs/design/SIGNAL_LIBRARY_2026-11-06.md). What signals say about the competitor sits beside it in competitors/<id>/signals.json, which only the projector writes.

id.description: The file name, and the subject of the signals about it

kind.description: competitor: a company whose offering can replace the venture's. alternative: what the customer does in its place, such as nothing, a spreadsheet or hiring someone. A record without it is a competitor

basis.description: What the claim that customers weigh this against the venture rests on: an interview record, a public source, or a guess no customer has confirmed

offering.description: What it is, in one or two plain sentences

for.description: Whom it is for, as its own pages say

price.description: Its published price, as stated on the page read

text.description: The price in the page's own terms, or that none is published

read.description: The date the page was read

does.description: What it does that bears on the venture's product

does_not.description: What its pages do not mention or its product does not do, next to the venture's product. Absence on a page is not proof of absence in the product

sources.description: The public sources read for this record

by.description: Who read it: a person's id or an agent's role

stance.description: How the venture stands toward it, in a person's words

next_move.description: What the competitor is likely to do next, read from its goals, assumptions, strategy and capabilities (Porter 1980, the four corners)

wrong_if.description: What would show the prediction wrong

created_from.description: The signal the projector created this record from, when a person did not write it first
